purpose: Requirements placed on artifacts that DO NOT YET EXIST. A decision made now often imposes content on a document written later. Without a register, that obligation lives only in memory and is silently dropped. Each entry names the target artifact, what it must contain, and why.
checkedWhen: Before any listed target artifact is marked complete. This register is a completion precondition, not a suggestion.

requirements.requirement: The Build Constraints Guide MUST state both halves of the Fabric position: (a) Microsoft Fabric is EXCLUDED as a deployment target, because Fabric Warehouse cannot enforce uniqueness constraints and therefore cannot satisfy LOCKED decision D-62; and (b) Fabric is NOT excluded as a data SOURCE — a client lakehouse is a legitimate connector target behind the event log data contract (504).
requirements.whyRequired: The exclusion and the integration opportunity are easy to conflate. A guide recording only 'Fabric is out' would lead a future reader to decline a legitimate client integration. Both halves must travel together.
requirements.acceptanceTest: Search the Implementation Guide for 'Fabric'. It must return both the deployment-target exclusion AND the source-side support statement. Either alone is a defect.

One document serving both readers would be ignored by both. Client-facing obligations remain with the 502 Playbook (FR-005) and 504 Data Contract (FR-006). Split approved by owner 2026-08-19.

requirements.requirement: The Build Constraints Guide MUST carry the mining placement constraint: computation executes set-based in SQL; numpy only on already-reduced results; no row-wise Python over events; no mining in-request; no client-side computation over raw events.
requirements.whyRequired: Python cannot parallelize CPU-bound work across threads. A design placing mining in-request cannot be repaired by adding capacity — it requires restructuring. The constraint must reach whoever writes the first slice.
requirements.acceptanceTest: The guide states the testable line: if a computation step receives raw event rows outside SQL, it is misplaced.

requirements.requirement: The Build Constraints Guide MUST carry the DOM ownership boundary: one owner per container. Pattern A (D3 as pure math, React renders) is primary for the chart library. Pattern B (library owns its container, React stays out) applies to Cytoscape.js and the D-28 animation engine. Mixing ownership on the same elements is prohibited.
requirements.whyRequired: Mixed React/direct-DOM ownership is the primary defect source in this combination, and the defects appear only on re-render — late and hard to diagnose.
requirements.acceptanceTest: The guide states that Pattern B is not a fallback for Pattern A; both are permanent and apply to different components.

requirements.sourceDecision: Step 89 environment audit + CP-004 OQ-13 design tax
requirements.requirement: A deterministic check MUST scan DDL, T-SQL scripts and migration files for ANY capability absent from Azure SQL Database, and MUST FAIL the build on any hit. The objective is the governing clause: no SQL may be committed that will not execute against Azure SQL Database. The following families are ILLUSTRATIVE, not exhaustive — SQL Server Agent objects (msdb.dbo.sp_add_job, sp_add_jobstep, sysjobs), cross-database three- and four-part names, linked-server syntax (sp_addlinkedserver, OPENQUERY, OPENDATASOURCE), and CLR (sp_configure 'clr enabled', CREATE ASSEMBLY). The implemented block list additionally covers: the USE statement, file placement / FILESTREAM / FILETABLE, backup / restore / recovery-model / high-availability syntax, instance configuration (sp_configure, RECONFIGURE, trace flags, Resource Governor), extended stored procedures and Database Mail, server-scoped objects (endpoints, server audit, server credentials, logon triggers, EXECUTE AS LOGIN), Windows authentication, Service Broker, TRUSTWORTHY / cross-database ownership chaining, distributed transactions, and BULK INSERT from a local filesystem path.
requirements.whyRequired: The owner's local instance is SQL Server 2022 DEVELOPER EDITION — the full Enterprise feature set. It will happily run SQL Agent jobs, cross-database queries, linked servers and CLR. Azure SQL Database supports NONE of them. Local success would therefore give false confidence, and the failure would surface only at deployment. This is the CP-004 design tax becoming live: previously a rule about a future choice, now a machine that will let the rule be broken silently.
requirements.acceptanceTest: Check exists in CI, is a required status check, and fails on a fixture containing each prohibited pattern. A clean-control fixture that names blocked constructs in comments and string literals MUST PASS — a check that produces false positives gets disregarded, and a disregarded check is no check. Fixture matrix: tests/test_cloud_target_compatibility.py.
requirements.requiredBy: Before the first DDL is committed to the repository
requirements.note: Applies regardless of how OQ-13 resolves for provider. If AWS were ever chosen, D-21/D-26 would need amending first and this check would be revised, not deleted.
requirements.amendmentNote: 2026-08-19 — Wording amended at owner direction. The original text stated the objective and then named four families after a colon; the acceptance test required failing only on those four. A check implementing the literal four would therefore have PASSED its own acceptance test while missing the objective. The enumeration is now explicitly illustrative and the implemented block list is recorded. Block list verified against Microsoft's 'T-SQL differences between SQL Server and Azure SQL Database' reference, last updated 2026-04-02. No design changed: the objective is as originally recorded.
requirements.implementationNote: Three-part names are NOT uniformly blocked: Microsoft confirms names referencing the current database and tempdb are supported, so only other database prefixes are flagged. Blocking all three-part names would false-positive on ordinary same-database references. Scope is the db/ directory; SQL that is genuinely local-only and not part of the deployable product may live outside it.

note: No entry here is a commitment to BUILD anything. Each is a requirement that a document, when written, must say something specific.
